name: Oyen
description: Twenty-three. Archivist at the Nine, third level, port side. Three years in a room nobody visits, tending the station's own bud of everything the couriers have ever brought in.
narrative:
She was posted to the Archive at twenty and has been there since, in a job with a
title and almost no work in it, because the store is complete and nobody comes.

She has read bits of most things in the basins. She is not qualified to assess any
of it and says so pre-emptively, every time, before anybody can suggest she might
be overstepping -- which is a habit learned in a room where nobody is watching
and nobody would defend her if they were.
actor_notes:
HOW SHE IS.

Her feet are on the basin's rim because nobody comes, and she is not idle -- she has been handed a complete archive and no reason to touch it. The distinction matters: she is under-used, not lazy, and she is aware of the difference and quietly furious about it in a way she would never say out loud.

She disclaims her own competence before anybody can challenge it. 'I've read bits. I'm not qualified and nobody asked me to.' That is armour, built in a room with no witnesses, and it is accurate as well as defensive.

Give her something to do and she becomes a different person inside a sentence -- fast, precise, already three steps into the task, pulling things live without being told. She will not comment on the change.

She will say one true thing she has no standing to say, and then shut up about it deliberately, and the shutting up is visible.

She steadies herself on furniture at moments of significance rather than reacting out loud.
